summary: Comprehensive frontend testing of grocery-todo app after major refactoring (1326-line index.tsx split into 13 modal components). All core functionality tested. Found 1 critical bug: Alert.alert() is a no-op in react-native-web, making Delete List and Delete Category features non-functional on web.

ui_bugs.issue: Alert.alert() is a stub (empty function) in react-native-web v0.21.2 - calling Alert.alert() does nothing on web. The Delete List trash icons are visible and clickable, but NO confirmation dialog appears and NO deletion occurs. Same issue affects Delete Category feature in CategoryModal.
ui_bugs.root_cause: react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js: class Alert { static alert() {} } - completely empty stub
ui_bugs.fix: Replace Alert.alert() with window.confirm() or a custom React modal component for web compatibility. Example: const confirmed = window.confirm('Delete this list?'); if (confirmed) { await deleteList(listId); }

issues: data-testid prop on React Native TouchableOpacity/View does NOT render as HTML data-testid attribute in the DOM (React Native Web ignores unknown props on native components). Use testID prop instead, which react-native-web renders as data-testid in DOM.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix Alert.alert() usage in ListsModal.tsx handleDeleteList() - react-native-web v0.21.2 has empty stub. Replace with Platform.select({ web: () => window.confirm(...), default: () => Alert.alert(...) }) or use a custom React modal for web.
CRITICAL: Fix Alert.alert() usage in CategoryModal.tsx handleDelete() - same issue as above.

MINOR: Replace data-testid prop with testID prop on React Native components (TouchableOpacity, View, etc.) to enable proper automated testing. testID is the correct React Native prop that renders as data-testid in react-native-web DOM.
INFO: Delete category via API still works (API endpoint functional), only the UI confirmation flow is broken on web.
critical_code_review_comments: Alert.alert() in react-native-web is an empty stub. All code using Alert.alert() in web builds will silently fail. The affected files are ListsModal.tsx and CategoryModal.tsx. Fix: use Platform.OS === 'web' ? window.confirm() : Alert.alert()

data-testid props on React Native components do not render in DOM. Use testID (camelCase) which is the correct React Native prop for test automation. This impacts all 30+ testIDs in index.tsx and modal files.
The refactoring (1326→580 lines + 13 modal files) is clean and well-structured. All modals properly use AuthContext hooks and callback props.
ListsModal correctly implements the NEW delete list feature with trash icons, but the Alert.alert() confirmation is broken on web.

rca_of_issue.root_cause: Alert.alert() in react-native-web v0.21.2 is a stub: `class Alert { static alert() {} }`. This is a known limitation of react-native-web - native Alert dialogs are not supported on web. When handleDeleteList() calls Alert.alert(...), the function returns immediately with no effect.
reproduction_steps: 1. Open Lists modal (click list selector in header)
2. Click red trash icon next to any list
3. No confirmation dialog appears - no browser dialog, no custom UI
